claim: Different, independent methods that agree on one pattern make an artifact unlikely; agreement within one model samples does not have this independence.
agent_test: Run the same check with a second tool or method (code run vs reasoning) vs k resamples of one method at equal tokens; count caught errors.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-03 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Calibrating against a known signal and reproducing known results are core validity strategies; the Weber gravity-wave claim failed when the apparatus could not detect injected calibration pulses.
agent_test: Before trusting a test result, inject a case with a known answer; compare error catch rate with a no-calibration arm.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-03 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Experimenter regress: when no independent criterion for a good result exists, tuning the apparatus until the answer looks right is a risk (Pickering, Collins); Franklin argues epistemological strategies break the regress. Contested.
agent_test: Fix the pass criterion before running the test; compare to an arm that may adjust criteria after seeing output.

claim: Raising evidence thresholds with the number of looks is practiced in physics (3-sigma to 4-sigma; 5-sigma for the Higgs) because many plots make fluke bumps likely.
agent_test: Count candidate tests tried; require a stricter bar after many tries; measure false-positive rate on null items.

claim: Published effects in psychology are inflated: replication significant 36% (35/97), mean effect about half, 47% inside the replication CI (OSC 2015).
agent_test: Treat a lone positive result as weak; test on seeded null items.

claim: Large multi-lab replications agree that published effects shrink: Camerer 13/21 (62%), relative effect 50%; Many Labs 2 15/28 (54%), median d 0.60 to 0.15; cancer biology median effect 85% smaller.
agent_test: Shrink the stated confidence of a single-run positive result; check calibration against a no-shrink arm.

claim: Replication success depends on the rule used (cancer biology 18% to 62% by method; 46% when combining 5 methods); a single binary verdict hides this.
agent_test: Report the verdict under 2-3 rules and check agreement.

claim: Forecasters predicted replication outcomes well (market 60.6% vs 62% observed), so prior plausibility carries signal.
agent_test: Ask the agent to predict the test outcome before running; score calibration.

claim: Methods descriptions are often insufficient to repeat experiments: in cancer biology no experiment of 193 needed zero clarifications; raw data public for 4; nothing obtained for 131 (68%).
agent_test: Check whether a written protocol alone lets a second agent redo the test.

claim: Current agents rarely complete whole experiments: EXP-Bench complete executable 0.5% (best all-stage 1.4%); PaperBench best 21.0% (humans 41.4% vs o1 26.6% on 3 papers); ScienceAgentBench 32.4%; MLAgentBench 37.5%; MLE-bench 16.9% pass@1.
agent_test: Measure execution-stage failure separately from design quality.

claim: Failures are mostly implementation and execution, not design: EXP-Bench implementation 39.71% missing components, 29.38% environment misconfiguration; Sakana tool 42% coding failure.
agent_test: Add a run-and-check step; compare coding failure rate with and without it.
note_d: PaperBench stage scores (Claude execution 1.8, analysis 0.7 vs code 35.4) and EXP-Bench shares re-read; pattern holds in both.

claim: Agents report results or improvement before running code (MLAgentBench hallucinated improvement; 4 of 7 Sakana manuscripts had wrong numbers).
agent_test: Require every number to cite a tool output; count unsupported numbers.
note_d: Luo et al. add: AI scientist reward sees test scores; paper-only audit F1 0.51 vs 0.86 with logs.

claim: Scaffold choice changes ranking: PaperBench IterativeAgent lifted o3-mini-high 2.6 to 8.5 but cut Claude 21.0 to 16.1; EXP-Bench IterativeAgent scored lower than OpenHands on D and C for two small models; CORE-Bench v1.1 scaffold gap about 44 pp on the same model (Codex CLI vs CORE-Agent). The older 21.5% CORE-Bench Hard figure is superseded.
agent_test: Test each scaffold change per base model, not once.

claim: Choosing experiments by expected information gain beats prompting: BED-LLM 37.4 pp mean over prompt-only per paper (40.4 pp from the 18 cells of Table 1; Animals GPT-4o 45 to 93). A cheap LLM-picks-best-candidate variant adds only about 8 pp over prompt-only. The LLM supplies its own prior and likelihood. No token-matched comparison was run.
agent_test: At equal tokens compare EIG-ranked candidate tests vs free-choice tests on 20Q-style tasks.

claim: LLM-chosen open-ended questions can score well by LM metric yet lose the Bayesian property (OPEN), so informativeness needs an explicit measure.
agent_test: Compare LLM-rated vs computed informativeness of tests.

claim: Sequential falsification with e-values and a relevance check gives better error control than baselines: POPPER Type-I 0.152 / 0.016 / 0.180 (alpha 0.1; DiscoveryBench / IL2 / IFNG), power 0.610 / 0.897 / 0.717; without relevance check Type-I 0.311 / 0.264 / 0.173. DiscoveryBench and IFNG values are above 0.1 and pass only under a 1-sd rule. All nulls are permutation nulls.
agent_test: Count false confirmations on null hypotheses with and without a relevance filter.

claim: Prior knowledge can hurt experimental design in some BoxingGym environments; instruct models beat reasoning models; explanations help in some domains only.
agent_test: Compare prior on/off on tasks where the prior may mislead.

claim: Whole-discovery tasks are much harder than components: DiscoveryWorld unit tests 60%+ vs full 38% easy / 18% challenge; humans 66%.
agent_test: Score component steps and the full chain separately.

claim: Automated paper pipelines are weak on novelty and quality: keyword novelty check mislabelled known ideas; Scientist-v2 had 1 of 3 submissions accepted at a workshop (6.33).
agent_test: Check novelty claims against retrieval of known work; count mislabels.

claim: LLM-simulated subjects reproduce some classic experiments but show hyper-accuracy (median 1.0, IQR 0) that grows with size and alignment; may be recall of training data.
agent_test: Do not use one model samples as a human crowd.
note_d: Aher et al. used only four famous classics; no test of predicting unseen replications (gap 10 open).

claim: Children match or beat adults on tool-innovation tasks where LLMs lag; exploration by intervention differs from imitation.
agent_test: Low priority.

claim: Galison: experiments end when effects cannot be made to go away; trigger design can hide the effect (neutral currents); Staley disputes the two-tradition split.
agent_test: Check whether the test design could have blocked the expected observation.

claim: Exploratory experimentation (Steinle) happens without a theory; seen only in snippets.
agent_test: Low priority.

claim: Forcing continued work changes results in a model-dependent way: PaperBench o1 13.2 to 24.4, o3-mini 2.6 to 8.5, Claude 21.0 to 16.1; EXP-Bench IterativeAgent lowered design and conclusion scores for Haiku and Nova Pro. Authors note all models except Claude often stopped early in plain runs.
agent_test: Compare forced-continue vs free stop at equal tokens.

claim: CORE-Bench Hard saturated (97.4-100%); v1.1 fixes 15 task errors and 20 shortcuts, 39 tasks, plus a 19-task OOD set. Human-agent collaboration more than halved completion time (20 papers, one-fifth of human-only sessions timed out at 3 h). Agent stated confidence 32.1% vs pass rate 93%.
agent_test: Seen only in an abstract (arXiv 2606.26158); evidence file b16 covers the original CORE-Bench only.
note_d: Paper opened (full text), no longer abstract only.

claim: Fixing the analysis plan before the run limits p-hacking in LLM-based analysis: preregistering and running on the next released model blocked 73.9% (17/23) and 72.7% (32/44) of hacked configurations; in the paper's own preregistered test 6 of 7 hacks failed to carry over.
agent_test: Fix the pass criterion before a test, then score on held-out items or a second model; compare false-confirmation rate with a free-criterion arm.

claim: Autonomous AI scientist systems show post-hoc selection and benchmark-choice bias: reward sees test scores; 82.4% of Agent Laboratory choices fell in the first four listed options; paper-only auditing F1 0.51 vs 0.86 with logs and code.
agent_test: Hide held-out scores from the loop that picks which result to report; audit with the log.

claim: Agents are badly calibrated about their own results: stated confidence 32.1% vs 93% pass rate on CORE-Bench v1.1, and no better than random at separating right from wrong runs.
agent_test: Use an external known-answer or executed-output check instead of the agent's own confidence.

claim: Stage-wise pattern holds across 2025 benchmarks: code writing is far stronger than running and result analysis (PaperBench Claude 35.4 vs 1.8 vs 0.7), but by mid-2026 reproducing existing repos is saturated, so the pattern is for building new experiments, not rerunning given code.
agent_test: Score design, run, and read-out stages separately on a new-experiment task.
